MIT Sloan Management Review research by Rollag, Parise and Cross reports external hire ramp times of eight to twenty six weeks or longer; this is old evidence from one financial services firm, not a software leadership benchmark. Additional disruption to existing developers is reserved for the separate onboarding risk. · Plausible range: −5 to 20 %/person, most likely 6 %/person

notes.text: Olumi's what-if for 'Change in Team delivery throughput per person added', not their figure: −5 to 20 %/person. Basis: Olumi estimate of cumulative delivery over the three month launch window, relative to the existing team's output. Assumes recruitment starts now and a typical external hire joins partway through the window. Leadership could unblock six mid weight developers, but hiring and learning the codebase limit the immediate gain. MIT Sloan Management Review research by Rollag, Parise and Cross reports external hire ramp times of eight to twenty six weeks or longer; this is old evidence from one financial services firm, not a software leadership benchmark. Additional disruption to existing developers is reserved for the separate onboarding risk.

notes.text: Olumi's what-if for 'Change in Team delivery throughput if developers grew by as many again as there are now', not their figure: −12 to 54%. Basis: Olumi estimate for a whole doubling of the current developer team, calibrated to the actual addition of two developers over three months. The two developer option receives one third of this effect. Recruitment and ramp up leave substantially less productive time than immediate fully effective staffing would imply, while the leadership gap remains. MIT Sloan Management Review research by Rollag, Parise and Cross reports external hire ramp times of eight to twenty six weeks or longer, based on an old study of one financial services firm. The wide range allows limited early contribution or unusually fast starts; existing staff onboarding disruption is reserved for the separate risk.

notes.text: Olumi's what-if for 'Change in Team delivery throughput per day/week added', not their figure: −4 to 10 % weeks/day. Basis: Olumi estimate for allocating one existing developer day each week to technical leadership throughout the three month window. Assumes a normal five day working week and that a capable mid weight developer can resolve some coordination and review bottlenecks. The direct loss of implementation time is included. Benefits could outweigh that loss across six developers, but unclear authority or limited leadership experience could leave a net reduction. No directly applicable published rate is available.

notes.text: Olumi's what-if for 'Chance: Onboarding absorbs existing developer time', not their figure: 70% to 99%. Basis: Olumi estimate of at least one material diversion of existing developer time into onboarding during the three month launch window, conditional on an external hire joining before launch. Codebase explanation, environment setup and review commonly require existing staff involvement, particularly without an established technical lead. Exceptionally strong documentation or a very late start could limit the diversion. No directly applicable published event frequency is available.

notes.text: Olumi's what-if for 'Share kept if it happens: Onboarding absorbs existing developer time', not their figure: 0.35 to 0.95. Basis: Olumi estimate of the share of the projected throughput change retained if material onboarding demands occur during the three month window. This multiplies the incremental throughput change, not the existing team's total output. Assumes routine mentoring and review absorb some expected gains, with heavier demands for two simultaneous hires and lighter demands for an experienced lead. The broad range reflects unknown documentation, codebase complexity and arrival dates. Hiring delay and the new hire's own ramp up are already included in the throughput estimates.
